overview: The Medford Energy and Environment Committee discussed climate plan monitoring, municipal sustainability initiatives, and a proposed biweekly trash collection program. The committee also approved sending a letter opposing state funding cuts to Mass Save.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes of the previous meeting as amended to correct staff attendance.

items.title: City Staff Updates
items.summary: Brenda Pike shared updates on Electrify Medford outreach, upcoming EV charger installations, citywide cleanup events, MVP grant applications, and a report on predatory electric suppliers.

items.title: Climate Action Monitoring
items.summary: Josh Ekhart-Lee led a discussion on tracking implementation of the Climate Action and Adaptation Plan, with members offering feedback on how to streamline data collection and member involvement.

items.title: Discussion on Proposed Biweekly Trash Pickup
items.summary: Committee members raised concerns regarding a proposed biweekly trash collection schedule, discussing potential sanitation issues, compliance, and state regulations.

items.title: Mass Save Advocacy Letter
items.summary: The committee approved sending a letter to state legislators opposing proposed cuts to Mass Save funding, incorporating minor revisions.

items.title: Zero Waste and Urban Forestry Updates
items.summary: Members received updates on upcoming zero-waste events, including a clothing swap and free flea market, as well as tree giveaways and findings from the Urban Forestry Management Plan.
